contributions.implementation_detail: A lightweight pixel-level modeling network is presented, which operates at full resolution to model pixel-wise features without downsampling, and combines base and detail components through a gated module to generate the fused image directly.

contributions.improvement: efficient image feature extraction and reduced computational burden
contributions.implementation_detail: A lightweight architecture incorporating dense CNN and Mamba without downsampling operations is designed for efficient image feature extraction. Additionally, a gated output module leveraging base and detail components is introduced to generate the fused image on a pixel-by-pixel basis. An axis decomposition method and an optimized state space model Mamba are used instead of the Transformer.

contributions.improvement: improved fusion performance
contributions.implementation_detail: An additional supervised task involving the random masking based image reconstruction is introduced to augment the unsupervised image fusion task.

contributions.improvement: superiority and robustness
contributions.implementation_detail: The proposed LPM-Net is evaluated on brain, neck, heart and prostate datasets against other mainstream image fusion methods to verify its superiority and robustness.

limitations: The method is specifically designed for the fusion of well-registered multi-modal medical images. When dealing with misregistered or unregistered image pairs, the method may struggle to effectively identify corresponding features, leading to sub-optimal fused results.

When fusing noisy and low-resolution ultrasound images and PET images, the presence of noise and fuzzy details in these source images hampers the effectiveness of the gradient-based loss function in enhancing the fusion effect.

experiment_setup.training_details: Multi-modal training images from the Harvard dataset were randomly cropped to 128x128, while WHU-MRI-PET training images were cropped to 256x256. Random horizontal and vertical flips, as well as rotations of 90°, 180°, and 270° were applied to mitigate overfitting. The network was trained using the AdamW optimizer on an NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU (24 GB RAM) and 5.20 GHz Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-12900K CPU with a batch size of 1. The learning rate was initialized at 1x10^-4 and gradually reduced to 1x10^-6 using a cosine annealing strategy. The network was trained for 100 epochs. Hyperparameters ξ1, ξ2, ξ3 and N were set to 1, 10, 10, and 64, respectively. For MRI-CT fusion, loss function coefficients ξ1, ξ2, and ξ3 were empirically determined as 1, 1, and 10. For MRI-PET and MRI-SPECT fusion, pseudo-color PET/SPECT images were first transformed from RGB to YCbCr space (Formula 14); the Y channel was fused with the MRI image, while Cb and Cr components were recombined and converted back to RGB space.

experiment_setup.training_details: The networks are trained by gradient descent implemented by AdamW optimizer with a learning rate initialized as 3 x 10^-4, which decreases to 8e-5 using cosine annealing decay strategy if validation loss remains the same for 5 epochs. The stopping criterion is set as 10 epochs. The original HSIs are used as reference images, blurred by a 7x7 Gaussian filter (std dev 2) and downsampled by averaging over d x d pixels to synthesize LR-HSIs (d=4 or 8 for PLGC/Pavia, d=8 or 16 for CAVE/HARVARD). MSIs are used as HR-MSIs. LR-HSIs and HR-MSIs are cropped and normalized to [0, 1]. Training data augmentation includes random vertical/horizontal flip and 90-degree rotation, and patches are cropped to 128x128 or 256x256 pixels. The number of feature channels Nm is set to 24 for m=1,2. The binary switch τ in ICM is set to 0 for m=1 and 1 for m=2,3. All algorithms are implemented in PyTorch on Linux 18.04 with a single NVIDIA GeForce GTX 3090Ti GPU.
